title: My house sitter got married in my backyard
author: Storytime
hook: I hired a house sitter for two weeks. When I got home, my neighbors kept congratulating me on my wedding.
story: In September, I went to visit my sister abroad for two weeks. I hired a house sitter through an app. Her name was Paige, five star reviews, loved my cat. When I got home, the house was spotless. Cleaner than I'd ever left it. There were fresh flowers on the table. I thought, wow, best sitter ever. The next morning, my neighbor waved at me over the fence and said, congratulations, it was beautiful! I said, what was? She said, the wedding. I laughed, because I'm very single. Then another neighbor said it. And another. So I went to the backyard. There were tiny holes in the lawn in two perfect rows. Like chairs had been set up. And a single white ribbon stuck in my rose bush. I searched Paige's name online. And there it was. Her wedding album. In my backyard. Under my apple tree. Her caption said, married at our dream home. Sixty guests. She'd told everyone it was her house. Her new husband thinks so too. And her photographer just tagged my address. Part two?
caption: congratulations on my wedding I guess 💒 #storytime
sound: a sweet wedding piano that turns comedic at very low volume
why: House sitter horror stories are trending, the spotless house and fresh flowers mislead viewers, the neighbors' congratulations are a hilarious reveal, and the tagged address sets up part two.

title: Grandpa's Thanksgiving announcement
author: Storytime
hook: At our early Thanksgiving dinner, my grandpa stood up and announced he's getting remarried. To my ex's grandmother.
story: My grandpa Joe is eighty one. Since my grandma passed three years ago, he's been pretty lonely. This spring he started going to a dance class at the community center. He suddenly had a lot of energy. New shirts. A new cologne. We figured he'd found a friend. Last night, at our early family Thanksgiving, right after the turkey, he tapped his glass and stood up. He said, I have an announcement. I've met someone wonderful, and she said yes. Everyone cheered. My aunt cried. Then he said, she's coming for dessert, actually. The doorbell rang. And in walked Margaret. I knew Margaret. I'd spent three Christmases at her house. Margaret is the grandmother of my ex girlfriend, Emily. Emily and I broke up a year ago. Badly. Margaret hugged me and said, oh, sweetheart, it's so lovely to see you. Then she whispered, Emily is the maid of honor. The wedding is in March. Grandpa wants me to be his best man. Which means I'll be standing next to my ex, at the altar, for the whole ceremony. Do I say yes?
caption: grandpa found love. with my ex's grandma 🦃 #storytime
sound: a warm, old-school swing tune with a comedic twist at very low volume
why: Dinner table announcements are a classic Thanksgiving viral format, grandpa's new cologne is the planted clue, and the best man dilemma gets everyone commenting.

title: The nanny job ad
author: Storytime
hook: A dad offered me ten dollars an hour to nanny four kids, cook, and clean. Then I met the mom.
story: I've been a nanny for six years. Last month, I saw a job post. Four kids. Cooking, cleaning, homework help. Ten dollars an hour. I almost scrolled past. But I needed work, so I agreed to one trial day. The dad, Greg, met me at the door. He was very clear. Don't discuss pay with my wife. She hates talking about money. At lunch, the mom, Laura, came home early. She was so sweet. She said, I'm so glad the agency sent you. Thirty-five an hour is a lot, but you're worth it. I froze. There was no agency. Greg had told Laura he hired me through an expensive nanny agency. She was transferring him thirty-five dollars an hour. He was paying me ten. And keeping the rest. Laura saw my face and asked, is everything okay? Greg was standing right behind her. Shaking his head at me. I said I'd let her know after the trial. That was yesterday. Laura just texted me asking if I'll start Monday. Should I tell her?
caption: the agency was him 💸 #storytime
sound: a tense, ticking suspense beat at very low volume
why: Nanny job horror stories are trending, the don't discuss pay rule is the planted clue, and the should I tell her question pulls strong opinions.
